hypothesis: Pilot correction margins remain below baseline prior; test longer training and a matched higher learning rate without changing exploration or representation.
diagnosticSummary: 48 sampled training-range games: action mean prior 5.666 vs mean strongest alternative correction advantage .525 (maximum 1.930); skillChoice mean correction -.064. This does not establish a causal bottleneck or that raising learning rate improves strength.
initialization: Identical parent weights; both arms fresh Adam and RNG, explicit new curriculum, not optimizer-preserving resume. Retain initial and final snapshots.

evaluation.stage: development screen, all arms reported; not final acceptance or proof of single-parameter causal effects across training randomness

reward: Terminal team win/loss only; no entropy or intermediate reward
followup: Inspect final strength and decision departures. Expand promising candidates to the 18-seed balanced development schedule before considering frozen independent final evaluation. A failed arm remains in reports; no automatic deployment.

developmentExpansion.trigger: Both final arms improved in preregistered six-seed screen; evaluate BOTH unchanged checkpoints, do not choose only the favorable arm.
developmentExpansion.note: Reused development range including initial six seeds; not independent confirmation. Independent final seeds remain unused. Workers increased only after fixed-model throughput checks; compare overlapping raw scenarios for replay consistency.
